title: Return labels expose customer shipping rate and never selected label cost

acceptanceCriteria.description: PrepShip rejects missing, inactive, or zero return-customer pricing before Client Portal can invoke a postage provider.

Customer DTOs, return workflows, Billing, and UI consume only backend-frozen customer shipping money and do not disclose selected label cost, provider cost, carrier identity, or renamed internal-rate fields.
Return Billing consumes the frozen return customer shipping rate, skips missing truth for reconciliation, and never falls back to selected, label, house, or other provider cost.
Existing policy-versioned frozen snapshots remain immutable; retries and completed-label recovery return the same canonical customer amount without a second purchase.
A read-only audit classifies unsafe historical snapshots and Billing mismatches without offering a production repair or mutation path.

PrepShip focused rate, Billing, return-row, strict typecheck, and production build checks; all 156 Client Portal guards; strict typecheck/build; and CP-043, CP-045, and CP-057 disposable-database integrations pass at the reviewed commits.

canonicalOwners: src/services/customer-shipping-money.ts owns return customer policy validation, preview, and immutable final freeze
src/services/billing-shipping-line.ts owns canonical customer shipping amount calculation
Client Portal src/services/returns.ts fences provider mutation and delegates customer pricing to PrepShip
Client Portal returns.return_customer_shipping_rate is the frozen customer-safe Billing and display value

oldOwners.path: PrepShip zero-markup label-cost fallback used by return freeze
Client Portal post-purchase customer-money freeze ordering
Client Portal return Billing raw shipment cost projection

wrappers.delegatesTo: the scoped PrepShip return-preview and freeze endpoints

sotBypass.details: PrepShip decides customer shipping money. Client Portal forwards provider candidate facts server-to-server, receives a customer-safe amount and provenance, and contains no pricing formula or raw-cost fallback.
